metadata.title: Write a reverse-proxy incident handover
metadata.topic: Web-Service Diagnosis — Offline Evidence (Simulator / Offline snapshots)

mission.brief: Correlate a proxy failure with a scoped upstream connection result without asserting an unproved cause. Select the four incident=WEB-4 records and sort their fixed-width UTC timestamps. Exclude the other incident. Equal timestamps use bytewise full-record order, not an inferred causal order. Save the required factual records in report.txt and display the final report with cat. Self-review the interpretation and next checks in HELP.txt.
constraints: SIMULATOR / OFFLINE SNAPSHOTS: fictional supplied evidence, not live measurements of your computer or VM. Read reference.txt for source excerpts and HELP.txt for context/model interpretation.
Automatic score checks exact factual report bytes (80) and final cat report.txt (20). Free-form reasoning, diagnoses and next checks are self-reviewed; 100/100 is not mastery.

Keep record spelling, order and final LF exactly; equivalent supported paths/filters are accepted, arbitrary report formatting is not normalized. Only report.txt is writable. > truncates first; failures do not undo writes. Finish all writes before the checked reading; any write clears prior reading evidence.

Challenge states the same factual requirements without a repair command. No service changes, live lookups, certificate validation, shell or network execution. Type help for supported commands; cat HELP.txt for this lesson reference.

hints: Compare the question with the supplied vantage points, timestamps and fields. Where did the observed request fail, and which cause remains a hypothesis?

Read reference.txt and HELP.txt. The proxy returned 502 while its logged upstream connection was refused; a nearby direct test from the proxy host also refused the same endpoint. The no-URI proxy_pass form preserves this simple request URI. These records support an upstream connection failure, not a confirmed crash, bad deployment, firewall rule or later recovery. Check scoped listener/process/configuration evidence next. Select only the required records; do not add a causal conclusion to the scored factual report.
A supported construction is: grep -F 'incident=WEB-4' evidence.txt | sort > report.txt. Then cat report.txt. Interpret the result separately; this score checks facts and inspection only.

/home/learner/reference.txt.content:
Synthetic nginx configuration excerpt on maple-proxy:
server { listen 198.51.100.40:80; server_name portal.example.test; location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080; } }
Supplied client curl -i http://portal.example.test/health at 10:31 UTC: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway; exit 0 (no --fail)
Linux nginx error excerpt at 10:31 UTC: connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream, request: "GET /health HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://127.0.0.1:8080/health"
maple-proxy curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8080/health at 10:31:01 UTC: curl (7) Failed to connect: Connection refused
No service-process, listener or deployment logs supplied.

/home/learner/HELP.txt.content:
SIMULATOR / OFFLINE SNAPSHOTS — Write a reverse-proxy incident handover
Goal: Correlate a proxy failure with a scoped upstream connection result without asserting an unproved cause.
These original synthetic annotated records describe fictional hosts, not your computer or a VM. reference.txt gives realistic source excerpts; evidence.txt contains normalized records for extraction, not literal tool output. No ip, ping, ss, dig, named-checkzone, curl, openssl, Apache or nginx command executes here.
Task: Select the four incident=WEB-4 records and sort their fixed-width UTC timestamps. Exclude the other incident. Equal timestamps use bytewise full-record order, not an inferred causal order.
Report format: preserve the selected record spelling, order and final LF exactly. Equivalent supported filters and paths are accepted; alternative prose/formatting is not normalized. Only report.txt is writable. Finish every write before cat report.txt; a later write invalidates reading evidence. Type help for the bounded text-command syntax.
Automatically checked: report facts (80 points) and displaying that final report with cat (20 points). No points for reading every source. A 100/100 score is NOT verified diagnostic reasoning or operational mastery.
Self-review questions: Where did the observed request fail, and which cause remains a hypothesis?
Model interpretation: The proxy returned 502 while its logged upstream connection was refused; a nearby direct test from the proxy host also refused the same endpoint. The no-URI proxy_pass form preserves this simple request URI. These records support an upstream connection failure, not a confirmed crash, bad deployment, firewall rule or later recovery. Check scoped listener/process/configuration evidence next.
Common mistakes: Treating 502 alone as a specific cause; testing loopback on the client instead of the proxy; replacing the configured endpoint without requirements; claiming live changes or future recovery.
Reasoning, proposed next checks and causal claims are self-reviewed, not keyword graded. Challenge hides guided commands and hints; this conceptual reference remains available.
Reset restores sources/reports and starts a new attempt, preserving history. Resume retains report, pending input, mode and exact scenario identity. This complements real practice; no live configuration or network effect occurs.
